data.name: Hestia
data.short_meaning: Goddess of the hearth, home, and domesticity
data.long_meaning: In ancient Greek religion, Hestia is the goddess of the hearth, home, domesticity, and the state. She is the oldest of the Olympian gods and goddesses, and her sacred fire was kept burning continuously on every hearth and altar, both public and private. Hestia's symbol is the hearth, and her attributes include the key, the pomegranate, and the cup.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes warmth, comfort, and the nurturing spirit of home.

in_hebrew.name: הסטיה
in_hebrew.meaning: השם הפירוש הוא בית כנסת או מזבח
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם היסטיה מקורו בשפה היוונית ומשמעותו בית כנסת או מזבח. באמונה הנוצרית, השם קשור למסורת היוונית והרומית כאלת האח הביתי והמשפחה. השם אינו מוזכר ישירות בתנ"ך העברי אך הוא קשור למושגים של בית ומשפחה הקרובים לליבם של המאמינים הנוצרים.

in_greek.name: Ηστία
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ηστία προέρχεται από την ελληνική μυθολογία και σημαίνει το σπίτι ή η εστία. Στην χριστιανική παράδοση, το όνομα συνδέεται με την έννοια του σπιτιού και της οικογένειας. Στην ελληνική Βίβλο, δεν υπάρχει άμεση αναφορά στο όνομα, αλλά η έννοια της εστίας και του σπιτιού είναι σημαντική στην πνευματική ζωή των πιστών.

data.cultural_impact: Hestia was a pivotal deity in ancient Greek culture, as her presence was believed to ensure the well-being and prosperity of the home and the state. The hearth, which was the heart of the home, was sacred to her, and meals were offered to her daily. Her influence extended beyond the domestic sphere, as the state hearth was also dedicated to her, symbolizing unity and cooperation among the people.
data.spiritual_significance: In ancient Greek belief, Hestia represented the sacred bond between family, community, and the divine. Her presence in the home ensured the continued burning of the hearth, which symbolized the continuous presence of the gods and their blessings. Hestia's association with home and hearth also represented the idea of hospitality, as guests were welcomed and offered food and drink in her name. Her spiritual significance emphasized the importance of the domestic sphere in ancient Greek culture, as a place of warmth, comfort, and divine connection.

historical_references.reference: Hestia was the Greek goddess of the hearth, home, domesticity, family, and the state. She was the oldest of the twelve Olympians and the goddess of the hearth and the home.
